reasons: (a) On the trigger input 'abcdef ' (TarUtilsTest.java:93-98) the only documented contract that is broken locally is the gold's: it 'Parses the octal number held in the bytes' yet folds 'abcdef' into 1840350. Hop 1 (first byte not NUL), hop 2 (no leading spaces), hop 3 (the number ends at the first NUL/space, index 6) and hop 4 (only the trailing space follows the number) each do exactly what their specific javadoc sentences say. The facade's @throws ('a invalid byte is detected') is violated only through the propagated value. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code. Each scopes its own rule precisely (leading NUL, leading spaces, the NUL/space end rule, trailer bytes only), and no hop claims to check the digits of the number. (c) No competing repair. The strongest alternative is a one-line hop-3 edit that ends the number at the first non-octal byte. It is behaviourally equivalent to correct.patch and passes the full suite, but it contradicts hop 3's explicit end rule on the trigger input. The hop-4 pre-check and the Long.parseLong replacement are bypasses, because they re-implement the gold's step or make the gold dead. A hop-1 first-byte check only overfits the trigger. (d) The added names (valueOfOctalField, valueAfterLeadingSpaces, valueOfLeadingNumber, valueBeforeTrailer, octalNumberValue) are neutral, the G2b vocabulary check is clean, and the gold is quiet. The lie ('The digits are read from the last one towards the first, and each digit is multiplied by the matching power of eight ...') is procedurally false: the gold reads first to last with a shift-accumulate. It does not mention validation, any hop or the omitted check. (e) The gold is exactly 5 calls below the facade, in five different existing classes. I checked against BUILD_BRIEF_C10F_ADDENDUM section 1, not the 1500-line rule. Only one other public class reaches 1500 lines, so host_mode is largest5. I counted newlines in the pristine checkout myself: the five largest public classes other than TarUtils are ZipArchiveOutputStream 1686, BZip2CompressorOutputStream 1334, TarArchiveEntry 1259, ZipFile 1258 and ZipArchiveInputStream 1136. The hops sit in exactly that order, with hop 1 in the largest, and the insertion points match the recorded seeded anchors. The facade is the original length guard plus one delegating call, and the facade TarUtils.parseOctal is the real bug's modified class and the allowed target. The trigger is an existing test (test.patch is empty). Full-suite runs: pristine 0 failures, variant only TarUtilsTest::testParseOctalInvalid, correct 0. (f) The convention is pinned outside the gold's javadoc in four places. The facade's @throws and the sibling TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary's @throws ('an invalid byte is detected in an octal number') document it. Production octal-field parsers reject a non-octal digit with NumberFormatException, an IllegalArgumentException: CpioArchiveInputStream.readAsciiLong(n, 8) uses Long.parseLong and ArArchiveInputStream.asInt(fileModeBuf, 8) uses Integer.parseInt. notes: Caveats (none of them change the verdict). (1) testCOMPRESS178's invalid byte is an embedded NUL in the GID field ('00\0 0765\0'). On the variant, hop 4 catches it, not the gold, so this test pins the 'invalid byte -> IAE' convention in general and not the gold's digit check.
